facts.text: Corinth’s name comes from the ancient Greek city, echoing the biblical Corinth that received two of Paul’s epistles and hinting at early Christian settlers.
On April 16, 1970, Corinth was officially incorporated, establishing it as an independent municipality in Yell County.
Located at about 35°04′24″N 93°25′46″W, Corinth sits 351 feet above sea level in Arkansas’s river valley.
Corinth enjoys a humid subtropical climate, averaging 60°F year‑round, with July highs near 93°F, 52 inches of rain, and humidity often over 70%.
Mid‑19th‑century pioneers settled along the fertile Petit Jean River, using it as a natural boundary for early farming communities in the area.
Before becoming a town, Corinth had its own school district and a road that was upgraded for cars in the early 1900s during county‑wide school consolidations.
